thread.title: Apple: Looking Ahead to Big Buybacks, More Dividends - Barron's

title: Apple: Looking Ahead to Big Buybacks, More Dividends - Barron's
text:
David Marino-Nachison April 30, 2018 10:34 a.m. ET
There’s plenty to wonder about with Apple set to announce quarterly financial results Tuesday afternoon, including iPhone sales , the iffy HomePod , and the potential effects of a trade war with China. Barron’s
Jon Swartz covered those ably last week, so here’s one more topic: What’s the company going to do with all that cash? Newsletter Sign-up
Barron’s Next 50 company Apple (AAPL) could offer more details about what it plans to do with its massive cash hoard, which includes billions that was being held overseas and will now be repatriated. “This is a very big deal to long-term investors,” one analyst recently told CNBC .
• Some of that will go to taxes, but the rest represents a wide range of possibilities. In a Sunday note, RBC Capital Markets offered its theory: Expect the not-entirely unexpected. Apple “is likely to maintain a mix between buyback and dividends while keeping some cash for possible deals,” they wrote.
On Monday, Synovus Trust’s Daniel Morgan estimated that the company “repurchases $210B in shares and pays $52B in dividends over the next 3 years.” And BMO Capital Management expects “a 50% increase in dividend this year and next, as well as a tripled rate of buybacks.”
“This will allow the company to reach a net cash neutral position by the end of FY20,” BMO wrote. Illustration: BMO Capital Markets
• RBC doesn’t expect major M&A, though some market watchers have speculated that the company might explore ways to accelerate its push into original content in a bid to tackle companies such as Netflix and Amazon.com . That might make them theoretically interested in a studio, a topic the Hollywood Reporter recently explored .
“Historically, Apple has been a platform for distributing content but increasingly they want to create their own content and that changes their whole profile,” analyst Gene Munster recently told the Guardian .
• And while CEO Tim Cook has said that megadeals aren’t the company’s style, that hasn’t squashed speculation about possible purchases of Walt Disney (DIS) or Netflix.
Shares of Apple were up more than 2% in early Monday morning action, while the S&P 500 was roughly flat. The stock is up about 3% in 2018, trailing the Barron’s Next 50 and the S&P 500.
